verdict.rationale: React's docs describe a component model where data is passed in and the UI is re-rendered to match. When the user interacts, new data is passed down rather than synced through bindings. React Developer Tools let developers inspect props and state, which supports tracing state changes. However, the pack never explicitly documents one-way data flow or contrasts it with two-way binding, and it has no independent corroboration that debugging is more predictable. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of unidirectional data flow (state lifted up, props down, callbacks up), an explicit contrast with two-way binding, and hands-on or community evidence that tracing state changes is easier.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace state changes through explicit, predictable data flow instead of debugging implicit two-way bindings

citations.quote: React components receive data and return what should appear on the screen. You can pass them new data in response to an interaction, like when the user types into an input.
React will then update the screen to match the new data.
Build encapsulated components that manage their own state, then compose them to make complex UIs.
Use React Developer Tools to inspect React components, edit props and state, and identify performance problems.
